name: Build Your Own Strategy
narrative:
The Snake Corridor repeats the same small manoeuvre: turn into an open side, then move forward. Writing those two actions again and again would make the policy difficult to read.

Use the Functions tab to name that sequence. Rules still decide when the sequence is appropriate; the function only describes the actions to perform.
objective: Solve the 11×11 Snake Corridor and use at least one custom multi-step function.
learningObjective: Separate decisions from reusable behaviour: rules choose a function, while functions run a fixed sequence one action per tick.
intelligenceExplanation:
The starting brain provides four primitive bricks and no rules. Because Functions is unlocked, you can compose a reusable sequence such as `pivot-left` followed by `step`.

The rule decides when to call it. The engine then checks each primitive against a fresh observation, so an unsafe step interrupts the sequence and lets the rules choose again.
hint: Compose `turn-left-and-step` from `pivot-left` and `step`, then call it only when the left side is open.
hints: Functions sequence actions; they do not contain WHEN checks. Keep sensing and branching in the rule list.
Create a two-step function: pivot-left, then step.
Use this order: atGoal → hold; !wallLeft → your turn-and-step function; !wallAhead → step; always → pivot-right.
brief: Build a reusable cornering function and use ordered rules to solve the Snake Corridor.
context: Rules decide when to act; a custom function packages a fixed action sequence.
